Iteration 11/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units

record.narrative: All returned estimates were read as signed to the registered claim direction, so the signed lower bound was compared with the +0.15 composite-unit threshold. H146 tests the broader MSI-high-free TP53-loss by KEAP1-loss interaction. Its signed estimate is +0.138 with interval -0.057 to +0.333, so it neither accepts a threshold-level positive interaction nor rejects the possibility because the upper bound still spans threshold. Combined with the prior clean TP53-KEAP1 interaction validation result, which was near zero and inconclusive, this does not support adding a TP53-KEAP1 interaction to the accepted architecture; it is closed as unresolved. H147 gives the clean-background CDKN2A-loss main effect signed estimate +0.167 with interval +0.110 to +0.224. It excludes zero but does not clear the threshold, so the most honest status is unresolved. The interval suggests a small real CDKN2A-loss association, but the lower bound below threshold prevents accepting a scientifically meaningful predictor. I defer rather than close it because it is biologically plausible and the only new near-threshold secondary predictor, although an adjusted independent validation would likely be wide and may not decisively clear threshold. H148 and H149 are rejected because the signed intervals are entirely below the threshold on the favorable side: MTAP-loss does not support a threshold-level CDKN2A-loss interaction and ARID1A-loss does not support a threshold-level modification of SMARCA4-loss. H150 and H151 are unresolved because their intervals include zero and also include threshold, despite small positive point estimates and no evidence of a meaningful positive interaction; these threads are closed as unpromising. H152 is accepted: in the dominant Avana-library, TP53-loss-free population, PTEN-loss has signed estimate +0.283 with lower bound +0.187 and valid cells, so it supports the conditional PTEN-loss stronger-dependency architecture in a technically robust library context. This is supplied-dataset association and does not add new independent validation, but it refines an already validated PTEN context. H153 is accepted and closed: within rare MSI-high cells, KEAP1-loss retains the expected weaker-dependency direction with signed estimate +0.794 and lower bound +0.552, although the small exposed cell warrants caution. H154 is also threshold-clear in rare MSI-high cells for SMARCA4-loss, signed estimate +0.658 and lower bound +0.445, but because it is a small rare-context estimate of a central driver association, I keep it active and request independent validation. No validation was requested for H146-H151 because the near-threshold or null intervals are unlikely to become decisive under adjusted independent validation, and the validated PTEN architecture already covers H152. These results remain observational associations in the supplied composite-dependency dataset, not causal or generalizable biological claims.

prompt:
Iteration 11/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
Final synthesis closes the two due validation decisions and records the evidence-supported supplied-dataset predictor architecture.

H133 is accepted and closed. The signed estimates are +0.754 discovery and +0.793 independent validation; because the claim direction is -1, the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is negative, meaning MSI-high cells have more negative dependency scores than MSI-high-negative cells in the clean eligibility background excluding TP53-loss, KEAP1-loss, SMARCA4-loss, and PTEN-loss. Both the discovery and adjusted validation lower bounds are far above the 0.15 composite-unit threshold, so this is not merely a marginal signal. It also shows that the MSI-high association is not explained by the currently accepted co-occurring TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, or PTEN contexts. The claim remains an observational association in this supplied dataset, not a causal statement or a claim that MSI-high has a general biological mechanism affecting composite dependency.

H154 is accepted and closed. Within rare MSI-high cells, SMARCA4-loss has signed estimates +0.658 discovery and +0.905 independent validation; direction -1 means the raw association is more negative dependency for SMARCA4-loss cells. The validation lower bound +0.482 exceeds the threshold despite strict adjusted uncertainty, so the rare-context threshold conclusion is supported. The cell sizes are small and the interval is wide, so the magnitude remains imprecise; however, the threshold conclusion is robust enough to close this active rare-context check. This refines the overall SMARCA4-loss association rather than creating a new biological claim: SMARCA4-loss remains associated with stronger composite dependency, and this pattern survives in a rare MSI-high context. It does not establish an interaction between SMARCA4-loss and MSI-high; the formal interaction tests remain unsupported or unresolved.

Supported supported findings now form a dataset-specific association map for the composite dependency endpoint. TP53-loss is associated with weaker dependency, meaning less negative composite scores, with discovery and validated positive signed effects around 0.42 and 0.35 units respectively, and with robust accepted estimates in Avana-library, lineage, batch, MSI-high-free, SMARCA4-loss-free, PTEN-loss-free, and KEAP1-loss contexts. KEAP1-loss is associated with much weaker dependency, signed effects around 0.83 in discovery and 0.77 in independent validation, with robust accepted estimates across TP53-loss-free, TP53-loss, SMARCA4-loss-free, Avana and non-Avana library contexts, lineage, batch, and the rare MSI-high context. SMARCA4-loss is associated with stronger dependency, meaning more negative scores, with overall discovery effect around 0.83 and independent validation around 0.82, and accepted estimates in TP53-loss-free, KEAP1-loss-free, adult, adenocarcinoma, Avana and non-Avana library, MSI-high-free, and rare MSI-high contexts. MSI-high is associated with stronger dependency, with discovery around 0.79 and independent validation around 0.87, and accepted estimates in clean backgrounds excluding other major accepted alterations and TP53/KEAP1-free or SMARCA4-free contexts. PTEN-loss is supported as associated with stronger dependency, but specifically in TP53-loss-free and related clean TP53-loss-free backgrounds; validation in the TP53-loss-free main context is around 0.30 with lower bound about 0.17. The overall PTEN-loss effect is not accepted as threshold-validated without the TP53-loss-free conditioning, so the defensible claim is conditional, not a general overall predictor.

Negative and unsupported findings are also scientifically informative. There was no threshold-level association for KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, STK11 loss, the constructed binary markers D/E/F, the overall Avana-versus-other library indicator, matched RNA-DNA availability, media serum, sex, SMAD4 loss, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, APC mutation, PIK3CA mutation, BRAF V600E, ERBB2 amplification, ARID1A loss, MTAP loss, RB1 loss, or the originally tested positive-direction PTEN claim. Many interaction or context-specificity hypotheses failed to support a meaningful modification: most lineage, batch, library, age, cas9 activity, ploidy, aneuploidy, hypoxia, growth-rate, screen-quality, MTAP, ARID1A, STK11, PIK3CA, and MSI interaction tests were rejected or left unresolved without supporting threshold-level modification. These are negative findings for those comparisons in this supplied dataset; they do not prove absence in other datasets.

Constructed signature results should remain clearly separated from biological interpretation. TP53-loss shows strong accepted differences by constructed research_signature axes, especially signature-B contexts, but these assays have no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role. Therefore those accepted results describe dataset-specific structure in a constructed assay space, not generalizable biology or mechanistic dependency.

Unresolved uncertainty remains primarily for secondary signals. The clean-background CDKN2A-loss test gave a signed estimate +0.167 with interval +0.110 to +0.224: it excludes zero but the lower bound is below 0.15, so it is not accepted as scientifically meaningful under the pre-specified threshold. I keep H147 unresolved but reopen the thread only to evaluate a newly registered MTAP-negative refinement. This refinement asks whether the CDKN2A-loss association survives when adjacent MTAP-loss is also excluded, which may isolate CDKN2A-specific structure or reveal that the earlier near-threshold signal is diluted or confounded by co-deletion context. It should be accepted only if its signed lower bound exceeds 0.15; it can be rejected if the signed upper bound is below 0.15; otherwise it should be closed as a trivial unresolved secondary signal. Other unresolved issues include the weak EGFR-amplification signal near zero, small non-Avana TP53-loss context, and TP53-KEAP1 interaction estimates near threshold that did not survive threshold or validation support. These unresolved points do not undermine the central validated architecture.

The most informative next analysis is therefore the registered CDKN2A-loss clean and MTAP-negative refinement. Independent validation would have been preferable for that near-threshold secondary predictor, but no voluntary validation requests remain. If this refinement clears the 0.15-unit threshold, it would add a minor secondary predictor; if not, the best conclusion is that CDKN2A-loss is at most a small non-threshold-associated feature and the supported architecture should remain limited to TP53-loss, KEAP1-loss, SMARCA4-loss, MSI-high, and conditional PTEN-loss contexts. All conclusions are dataset-specific observational associations with a composite dependency endpoint, not causal effects or generally applicable biological claims.

prompt:
Iteration 12/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

record.narrative: No assessments are due. I registered follow-up tests to resolve the only near-threshold secondary predictor, CDKN2A-loss, and to test biologically plausible co-alteration and technical-quality contexts without reopening major validated drivers as causal claims. The active clean MTAP-negative CDKN2A test remains registered, so I added a high-CRISPR-activity refinement, a MTAP-positive clean CDKN2A test to probe genomic co-deletion, and an MTAP-loss main effect in CDKN2A-loss-free clean cells to distinguish adjacent co-deletion from independent MTAP structure. I also refined PTEN-loss in TP53-loss-free PIK3CA-wild-type clean backgrounds to ask whether the accepted conditional PTEN signal is pathway-independent. For lung-biology-inspired secondary co-alteration hypotheses, I tested KRAS-mutation among STK11-loss cells, STK11-loss among KRAS-mutant cells, and RB1-loss among TP53-loss cells, all with expected raw more-negative dependency in the exposed co-altered context. I also tested reciprocal TP53-loss among RB1-loss cells as a major-driver robustness check. Finally, I tested TP53-loss, KEAP1-loss, and SMARCA4-loss within high screen_roc_auc cells to assess whether the accepted architecture survives in better-quality screens. All are signed to the claimed direction; threshold-level acceptance requires signed lower bound above 0.15, clear rejection requires signed upper bound below 0.15, otherwise unresolved. These remain observational supplied-dataset associations.

prompt:
Iteration 12/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

prompt:
Iteration 12/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: I audited each newly delivered signed Welch interval against the pre-specified +0.15 composite-unit acceptance rule: accept only when the signed lower bound exceeds 0.15, reject when the signed upper bound is below 0.15, and otherwise leave unresolved. All cells had valid cell sizes. The CDKN2A-loss block remains unresolved and near threshold rather than evidence-supported: H155 in the clean MTAP-negative background is +0.1532, 95% CI +0.0916 to +0.2149; H156 in high Cas9 activity is +0.1489, 95% CI +0.0505 to +0.2472; H157 in MTAP-loss-positive clean background is +0.2262, 95% CI +0.0769 to +0.3754. These intervals consistently exclude zero in the claimed direction in the cleaner tests, but their lower bounds do not exceed the 0.15 unit meaningful-effect threshold, and independent validation requests are no longer available. I keep H155 active only to evaluate a focused high screen_roc_auc clean MTAP-negative refinement; H156 and H157 are closed as unlikely to become decisive, and the older H147 thread is closed in favor of the H155 thread. H158 rejects the independent MTAP-loss stronger-dependency claim in CDKN2A-loss-free clean cells: signed estimate -0.0382 with signed upper bound -0.0012 is entirely on the unfavorable side of threshold and suggests a small raw direction opposite the claim. This is not evidence of biologically meaningful MTAP independence and likely reflects adjacent 9p21 co-deletion structure rather than a separate MTAP effect. H159 accepts conditional PTEN-loss in the TP53-loss-free, KEAP1-loss-free, SMARCA4-loss-free, MSI-free, PIK3CA-wild-type background: signed estimate +0.2561, lower bound +0.1710. This strengthens the conditional PTEN architecture and indicates the accepted PTEN signal is not dependent on PIK3CA-mutant cells, though it remains an observational supplied-dataset association. H160 and H161 are closed as unresolved because KRAS/STK11 reciprocal co-alteration intervals include zero and include threshold, providing no support for a threshold-level secondary interaction. H162 rejects RB1-loss as an additional stronger-dependency feature within TP53-loss cells: signed upper bound +0.0681 is below threshold. H163 accepts TP53-loss among RB1-loss cells as a robustness check for the already accepted TP53-loss weaker-dependency association: signed estimate +0.5441, lower bound +0.2931. The asymmetry versus H162 should not be overinterpreted as biology because the exposures, reference groups, and cell sizes differ. H164, H165, and H166 accept the major TP53-loss, KEAP1-loss, and SMARCA4-loss associations within higher screen_roc_auc cells, with signed lower bounds +0.3292, +0.6553, and +0.6905 respectively. These support dataset-specific robustness of the central architecture in better-quality screens but are subgroup descriptive checks, not causal or quality-adjusted causal effects. No validation request is possible because no new voluntary validation requests remain.

prompt:
Iteration 12/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
Due validation reassessment: H136 tested a positive interaction for TP53-loss among MSI-high-free, SMARCA4-loss-free, PTEN-loss-free cells: TP53-loss was hypothesized to be associated with a less negative composite dependency score more strongly when KEAP1 was lost than when KEAP1 was not lost. The signed discovery estimate was +0.1158 (95% CI -0.0926 to +0.3242), below the +0.15 unit lower-bound acceptance rule and not independently supportive. The scheduled independent validation was R131: signed estimate -0.0318 (adjusted interval -0.4035 to +0.3400). Because the estimate is signed to the claim direction, the raw independent-validation interaction was in the opposite direction and near zero. Although the adjusted validation interval is wide and technically still includes a positive threshold-level effect, the independent replication point estimate does not support the claimed positive interaction, and the original discovery estimate was already below threshold. I therefore reject H136 as a supported threshold-level interaction in this dataset. This is not a proof that no TP53-by-KEAP1 interaction is possible in any larger dataset, but within the available supplied-dataset and independent-validation evidence there is no reason to retain this specific interaction claim in the final predictor map. The investigation is closed.

Final supported supplied-dataset findings. The evidence-supported architecture for dependency_composite is dominated by four observational predictor groups, plus a more conditional fifth. First, TP53-loss is associated with weaker composite dependency, meaning a less negative dependency_composite score. The primary accepted claim H13 has signed discovery +0.4232 and independent validation +0.3549, both with lower bounds well above 0.15. This pattern was accepted or robustly reproduced in many supplied-dataset contexts, including Avana-library cells, adenocarcinoma cells, batch_a, MSI-high-free cells, SMARCA4-loss-free cells, PTEN-loss-free cells, KEAP1-loss-positive cells, RB1-loss cells, high screen_roc_auc cells, and several constructed-signature contexts. Second, KEAP1-loss is associated with much weaker composite dependency, also reflected by less negative scores. H14 has discovery +0.8315 and independent validation +0.7693; lower bounds far exceed threshold. KEAP1-loss was supported across TP53-loss-free, TP53-loss-positive, SMARCA4-loss-free, Avana and non-Avana library, adenocarcinoma, batch_a, MSI-high-free, MSI-high-positive, and high screen_roc_auc contexts. Third, SMARCA4-loss is associated with stronger composite dependency, meaning more negative scores. H62, signed direction -1, has discovery +0.8325 and validation +0.8166; raw exposed-minus-comparator differences were negative. Accepted SMARCA4-loss effects were observed in TP53-loss-free, KEAP1-loss-free, Avana and non-Avana library, adult, adenocarcinoma, MSI-high-free, high screen_roc_auc, and rare MSI-high-positive contexts. Fourth, MSI-high is associated with stronger composite dependency. H106, signed direction -1, has discovery +0.7918 and validation +0.8729, with validation lower bound well above threshold. H133 and H153/H154 further show that MSI-high-associated stronger dependency and SMARCA4-loss-associated stronger dependency are not abolished in clean or rare contexts. Fifth, PTEN-loss is supported only conditionally. The overall PTEN-loss claim H63 remains unresolved because its signed lower bound is below threshold despite positive point estimates. However, PTEN-loss was accepted as associated with stronger dependency, i.e. more negative scores, in TP53-loss-free and related clean backgrounds, especially H80, H94/H95, H107/H108, H131/H132, H152, H159, and other clean-cell checks. The strongest PTEN interpretation is therefore conditional: PTEN-loss-associated stronger dependency is visible mainly when TP53-loss and several other dominant alterations are absent, not as a uniformly unconditional predictor across all supplied cells.

Negative or unsupported findings are scientifically important because they narrow the predictor map. There was no threshold-level supported association for KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, STK11 loss, constructed markers D/E/F, the overall Avana-versus-other library indicator, matched RNA-DNA availability, media serum percentage, sex, SMAD4 loss, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, APC mutation, PIK3CA mutation, BRAF V600E, ERBB2 amplification, ARID1A loss, MTAP loss, or RB1 loss. The original positive-direction PTEN-loss overall claim was also unsupported. Many interaction hypotheses were rejected or left unresolved: most lineage, batch, library, age, Cas9 activity, ploidy, aneuploidy, hypoxia, growth-rate, screen-quality, MTAP, ARID1A, STK11, PIK3CA, and MSI interaction tests did not yield independently supported threshold-level modifications. The H136 validation failure adds a specific negative result for the TP53-by-KEAP1 interaction in a clean MSI/SMARCA/PTEN-free background.

Unresolved uncertainty remains mostly secondary. The clean-background CDKN2A-loss signal is near threshold but not accepted: H155 signed estimate +0.1532 (lower +0.0916) and related clean or high-quality refinements are close to but below the meaningful-effect lower bound. This suggests a possible small secondary association, but under the pre-specified threshold it should not be treated as an accepted scientifically meaningful predictor without stronger evidence. Small EGFR-amplification signals, non-Avana TP53-loss context estimates, and some near-threshold TP53-by-KEAP1 interaction estimates also remain unresolved or weak. H167 and H168 are useful active follow-ups if further discovery analysis is available: a high-quality clean MTAP-negative CDKN2A test and a high-quality clean PIK3CA-wild-type PTEN robustness test. These would be more informative than additional broad exploratory comparisons. If H167 clears the +0.15 lower-bound rule, CDKN2A-loss could become a minor secondary predictor; if it does not, CDKN2A-loss should remain an unresolved near-threshold signal rather than an accepted component of the final architecture.

All conclusions are observational associations in the supplied composite-dependency dataset. They do not establish causality, and they should not be interpreted as causal effects of TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, MSI-high, or PTEN states on biological dependency. The constructed research signatures and markers were useful structural probes but have no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role, so accepted signature-related structure remains dataset-specific assay geometry rather than generalizable biology. The final supported supplied-dataset claim set is therefore limited to: TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss associated with weaker composite dependency; SMARCA4-loss and MSI-high associated with stronger composite dependency; and PTEN-loss associated with stronger composite dependency conditionally in TP53-loss-free/clean backgrounds, especially independent of PIK3CA mutation status. The TP53-by-KEAP1 interaction claim H136 is not supported and is rejected.

prompt:
Iteration 13/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units

record.narrative: No assessments are due. At this explore stage I registered focused robustness and refinement tests rather than broad repeats of the accepted major-driver architecture. The goal is to test whether the supported predictor map remains threshold-level in important supplied-dataset contexts: batch_a, high screen_roc_auc cells, adult cells, rare MSI-high-positive cells for TP53-loss, and clean PIK3CA-wild-type backgrounds for PTEN-loss and CDKN2A-loss. These are falsifiable hypotheses about observational associations with dependency_composite only. For each claim, the returned estimate is already signed to the claim direction. I would accept only if the signed lower confidence bound exceeds the +0.15 composite-unit threshold, reject if the signed upper bound is below 0.15, and otherwise leave the claim unresolved. The SMARCA4-loss and MSI-high batch_a tests address whether the accepted stronger-dependency associations are robust to batch structure. The MSI-high screen_roc_auc test asks whether the MSI-high stronger-dependency association survives in better-quality screens. The TP53-loss test among MSI-high cells probes whether the accepted TP53-loss weaker-dependency association extends to the small MSI-high-positive context rather than only to MSI-free cells. The TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss adult/high-quality tests address age and screen-quality robustness without reinterpreting accepted main effects. The PTEN-loss clean PIK3CA-wild-type batch_a and adenocarcinoma tests examine whether the conditional PTEN-loss stronger-dependency signal is robust beyond the current accepted clean contexts, especially if it persists independent of dominant TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4/MSI alterations and PIK3CA mutation. The CDKN2A-loss clean MTAP-negative PIK3CA-wild-type high-quality test is a targeted refinement of the near-threshold CDKN2A thread; it asks whether the possible small stronger-dependency signal becomes threshold-level after removing MTAP co-deletion, PTEN loss, dominant drivers, MSI, and PIK3CA mutation and focusing on higher-quality screens. The EGFR-amplification test in a genetically cleaner background revisits a weak unresolved secondary predictor in a context less contaminated by major accepted drivers, with the expected raw direction being less negative dependency_composite. All conclusions remain dataset-specific observational associations and do not support causal claims or generalizability to other datasets.

prompt:
Iteration 13/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.
