Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction

record.narrative: No assessments are due, and no new validation requests remain. I registered 12 comparisons that extend the current evidence map in three ways: age-stratified robustness of the four major predictors, secondary PTEN-loss context dependence, and biomarker effect-modification tests. First, the four major accepted associations were accepted in many technical and genomic strata but not specifically in older individuals. Direct mean_difference tests for TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high in age_years >= 65 test whether the main effects persist when age is restricted to older adults. Expected raw directions are the same as the accepted main effects: positive for TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss weaker dependency, negative for SMARCA4-loss and MSI-high stronger dependency. Alternatives include attenuation due to age-related biology or selection bias from missing age, since age_years is not fully observed. Second, I registered has_rna_omics as a secondary technical availability predictor. The null main effect of has_matched_rna_dna has already been rejected, but RNA availability itself could reflect dataset selection; this is not a biological hypothesis, only a measurement-bias check. Third, I proposed biomarker interactions for the major predictors. For TP53 loss, an IFN-gamma-high stratum test with raw direction -1 asks whether immune/inflammatory cell state attenuates or reverses the TP53-loss weaker-dependency association. For KEAP1 loss, copy_number_8q24 ge 0 and growth_rate_doublings_per_day ge 0.5 test whether MYC-locus gain or higher proliferation augments the KEAP1-loss weaker-dependency association. For SMARCA4 loss, mutation_burden ge approximately the median and rnaseq_AXL_log2_tpm ge 3.0 test whether high TMB or AXL-related transcriptomic state strengthens SMARCA4-loss stronger dependency. For MSI-high, copy_number_8q24 ge 0 tests whether MYC-locus gain co-occurs with enhanced MSI-high stronger dependency. Finally, PTEN loss remains a secondary conditional predictor, and H204 remains active for PTEN loss by ploidy in clean cells; these new comparisons instead ask whether PTEN loss is stronger in high-TMB clean cells lacking the four dominant TP53-loss, KEAP1-loss, SMARCA4-loss, and MSI-high states. For all proposals, acceptance will still require the signed lower 95% bound to exceed +0.15 composite dependency-score units; rejection only when the signed upper bound is below +0.15; otherwise unresolved. These are dataset-specific observational comparisons, not causal claims or generalizable biological mechanisms.

prompt:
Iteration 16/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Conclusions remain dataset-specific observational associations.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No assessments are due, and no new validation requests remain. I registered 12 comparisons that extend the current evidence map in three ways: age-stratified robustness of the four major predictors, secondary PTEN-loss context dependence, and biomarker effect-modification tests. First, the four major accepted associations were accepted in many technical and genomic strata but not specifically in older individuals. Direct mean_difference tests for TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high in age_years >= 65 test whether the main effects persist when age is restricted to older adults. Expected raw directions are the same as the accepted main effects: positive for TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss weaker dependency, negative for SMARCA4-loss and MSI-high stronger dependency. Alternatives include attenuation due to age-related biology or selection bias from missing age, since age_years is not fully observed. Second, I registered has_rna_omics as a secondary technical availability predictor. The null main effect of has_matched_rna_dna has already been rejected, but RNA availability itself could reflect dataset selection; this is not a biological hypothesis, only a measurement-bias check. Third, I proposed biomarker interactions for the major predictors. For TP53 loss, an IFN-gamma-high stratum test with raw direction -1 asks whether immune/inflammatory cell state attenuates or reverses the TP53-loss weaker-dependency association. For KEAP1 loss, copy_number_8q24 ge 0 and growth_rate_doublings_per_day ge 0.5 test whether MYC-locus gain or higher proliferation augments the KEAP1-loss weaker-dependency association. For SMARCA4 loss, mutation_burden ge approximately the median and rnaseq_AXL_log2_tpm ge 3.0 test whether high TMB or AXL-related transcriptomic state strengthens SMARCA4-loss stronger dependency. For MSI-high, copy_number_8q24 ge 0 tests whether MYC-locus gain co-occurs with enhanced MSI-high stronger dependency. Finally, PTEN loss remains a secondary conditional predictor, and H204 remains active for PTEN loss by ploidy in clean cells; these new comparisons instead ask whether PTEN loss is stronger in high-TMB clean cells lacking the four dominant TP53-loss, KEAP1-loss, SMARCA4-loss, and MSI-high states. These are dataset-specific observational comparisons, not causal claims or generalizable biological mechanisms.","analyze":"No assessments are due and no validation requests remain. H191 is the highest-priority PTEN test because it asks whether PTEN-loss-associated stronger dependency persists in high screen-quality genetically clean MTAP-negative cells without requiring PIK3CA wild-type status. record.narrative: No assessments are due, and no new validation requests remain. I selected 12 previously registered active comparisons for analysis. H204 is the highest-priority focused follow-up because PTEN loss remains a secondary conditional predictor, and H204 directly tests whether the clean-background PTEN-loss association with stronger composite dependency is actually modified by ploidy rather than merely differing in precision across ploidy-stratified direct contrasts. H205-H208 test whether the four accepted major predictor associations persist in older adults, a demographic stratum not directly tested before. These include TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high. Decision rule remains prespecified: accept only when the signed lower 95% bound exceeds +0.15 composite dependency-score units in the claimed direction; reject only when the signed upper bound is below +0.15; otherwise leave unresolved. Iteration 16/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
I assessed the newly delivered discovery evidence with the prespecified signed-bound rule: accept only when the signed 95% lower bound exceeds +0.15 composite dependency-score units in the claimed direction; reject when the signed upper bound is below +0.15; otherwise leave unresolved. All estimates are already signed to the hypothesis direction, so they were not re-oriented.

H204 is the focused clean-background PTEN-loss interaction with higher ploidy. The signed interaction estimate was +0.0788 with interval -0.0785 to +0.2362. It does not clear the +0.15 lower-bound threshold, and it also is not precise enough to reject by the upper-bound rule. I therefore left it unresolved but closed the investigation because the point estimate is small, the comparison is already multiplicity-adjusted for the overall PTEN line, and no validation request is available. This result gives no support for the stronger claim that PTEN loss is materially modified by ploidy within the clean background; it should not be used to upgrade PTEN loss from a secondary conditional predictor to a major effect modifier.

The older-adult age strata were strongly informative. H205, TP53 loss in participants with age_years >= 65, was accepted: signed estimate +0.5181, interval +0.3176 to +0.7185. This supports persistence of the accepted TP53-loss association with weaker composite dependency in this older-adult subset. H206, KEAP1 loss in age_years >= 65, was also accepted: signed estimate +0.8313, interval +0.6453 to +1.0174, supporting the accepted KEAP1-loss association with weaker composite dependency. H207, SMARCA4 loss in age_years >= 65, was accepted: signed estimate +0.7205, interval +0.5281 to +0.9129, corresponding to the claimed stronger-dependency direction. H208, MSI-high in age_years >= 65, was accepted: signed estimate +0.8762, interval +0.6006 to +1.1517, also corresponding to stronger dependency. Together these age-stratified results materially increase confidence that the four major predictor associations are not confined to younger or non-older subsets within this dataset. However, age_years is missing for a substantial fraction of the sample, and the exposed cells are relatively small, especially MSI-high with 23 exposed cases. These are therefore dataset-specific observational associations subject to selection bias and age-missingness, not causal age effects or externally generalizable demographic claims.

The biomarker interaction panel mostly did not support effect modification. H210, TP53 loss by IFN-gamma state, was unresolved: signed estimate +0.1090, interval -0.0836 to +0.3016. It is centered near null and does not support a clear IFN-gamma-mediated modification of the TP53-loss association. I closed it as unresolved because the interval still technically spans the threshold, but it should not be treated as positive evidence. H211, KEAP1 loss by 8q24 copy-number state, was rejected: signed estimate -0.0239, interval -0.1548 to +0.1069; the signed upper bound is below +0.15, so it cannot support the claimed positive interaction. H212, SMARCA4 loss by high mutation burden, was unresolved: signed estimate +0.0949, interval -0.0364 to +0.2262. The point estimate is small and the lower bound is below zero; I closed it as unresolved but gave it no weight as evidence of TMB-related modification. H213, MSI-high by 8q24 copy number, was rejected: signed estimate -0.1343, interval -0.3695 to +0.1009. The interval does not support the claimed negative-interaction direction exceeding +0.15. H214, clean-background PTEN loss by high mutation burden, was rejected: signed estimate -0.0727, interval -0.2322 to +0.0869. This argues against meaningful PTEN-loss effect modification by TMB in the clean genetic background. H215, KEAP1 loss by higher growth rate, was rejected: signed estimate -0.1222, interval -0.2703 to +0.0259. H216, SMARCA4 loss by AXL expression, was unresolved: signed estimate +0.1146, interval -0.0180 to +0.2471. Like H210 and H212, it is near null and imprecise; I closed it as unresolved but did not treat it as evidence of AXL-mediated effect modification.

Overall, the new results strengthen the robustness of the four major predictor associations in older adults but do not support meaningful biomarker-based effect modification for IFN-gamma, 8q24 copy number, mutation burden, growth rate, or AXL expression in the tested predictor contexts. PTEN loss by ploidy also did not clear the interaction threshold. I therefore closed the age and interaction investigations and left no active PTEN interaction or CDKN2A follow-up. All conclusions remain within this supplied observational dataset and do not establish causality, mechanism, or generalizability.

There are also no response deadlines to reassess in this turn. The evidence map is therefore stable: it supports four large, direction-consistent, dataset-specific observational associations with dependency_composite, while leaving secondary and interaction claims mostly unresolved or negative.

Supported main associations, all above the 0.15 composite-unit meaningfulness threshold with signed lower bounds clear of the threshold and with independent validation for the main effects, are: TP53 loss is associated with a higher dependency_composite score, interpreted as weaker composite dependency (H13; discovery R1 signed +0.423, interval +0.327 to +0.520; validation R38 signed +0.355, interval +0.221 to +0.488). KEAP1 loss is likewise associated with weaker composite dependency (H14; discovery R5 signed +0.832, interval +0.766 to +0.897; validation R25 signed +0.769, interval +0.676 to +0.862). SMARCA4 loss is associated with a lower dependency_composite score, interpreted as stronger composite dependency (H62; discovery R32 signed +0.833, interval +0.767 to +0.898; validation R52 signed +0.817, interval +0.715 to +0.918). MSI-high is also associated with stronger composite dependency (H106; discovery R86 signed +0.792, interval +0.676 to +0.907; validation R105 signed +0.873, interval +0.685 to +1.060). These associations are not single-gene knockout interpretations; the endpoint is a composite dependency score.

The robustness within this supplied dataset is broad. The TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, and MSI effects were accepted in multiple genetic, technical, and quality-stratified subsets, including adenocarcinoma, Avana and non-Avana library contexts, high screen-quality cells, lower and higher ploidy, and several clean genetic backgrounds. The age_years >= 65 stratum added useful internal robustness: H205 TP53 loss signed +0.518, interval +0.318 to +0.719; H206 KEAP1 loss signed +0.831, interval +0.645 to +1.017; H207 SMARCA4 loss signed +0.720, interval +0.528 to +0.913; H208 MSI-high signed +0.876, interval +0.601 to +1.152. However, age_years is missing for a substantial fraction of records and exposed cells are smaller in the age-stratified tests, especially for MSI-high, so these are not causal age claims and should not be read as externally generalizable demographic effects. The accepted small MSI-high SMARCA4-loss association in H154, independently validated in R141, supports the SMARCA4 direction in a rare context but has small cell sizes and should not be treated as precise or externally generalizable.

PTEN loss remains a secondary, conditional finding. The overall main PTEN comparison does not clear the threshold after validation (H63; R36 lower +0.131; R65 lower +0.087), so I keep it unresolved overall. By contrast, PTEN loss is accepted in genetically cleaner backgrounds, especially in cells lacking TP53 loss and often also lacking KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, or MSI-high, such as H95, H94, H80, H131, H132, H152, H176, H182, and related accepted clean-context tests. This supports the view that PTEN-loss-associated stronger composite dependency can be detectable when dominant modifiers are absent, but it does not establish PTEN as a major unconditional predictor. The most relevant focused interaction, H204, tested PTEN loss by ploidy within a clean background and gave a small near-null signed estimate +0.079, interval -0.078 to +0.236, unresolved and closed. H214 tested clean-background PTEN loss by high mutation burden and was rejected. Together these argue against upgrading PTEN loss to a proven major effect modifier; it should remain context-dependent and precision-limited.

Negative or non-supportive findings are substantial. Repeated main comparisons did not support a meaningful difference beyond 0.15 in either claimed direction for KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, STK11 loss, ARID1A loss, MTAP loss, RB1 loss, SMAD4 loss, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, APC mutation, PIK3CA mutation, BRAF V600E, ERBB2 amplification, and clean-background EGFR amplification. The constructed research markers D, E, and F were not associated with meaningful dependency differences. Several technical or procedural variables also failed to show meaningful differences, including Avana versus non-Avana library, matched RNA-DNA availability, media serum percentage, and the tested sex comparison. These are dataset-specific non-support findings, not proof of exact zero effects.

Interaction or effect-modification evidence is mostly negative or inconclusive. Formal biological or biomarker interaction tests were generally near null and did not clear the threshold: KEAP1 by 8q24 copy number, MSI by 8q24 copy number, PTEN by high mutation burden, KEAP1 by higher growth rate, KEAP1 by hypoxia, SMARCA4 by ARID1A, SMARCA4 by growth-rate, and several ploidy or lineage modifiers were rejected. Other interactions were unresolved but not positive evidence, including TP53 by IFN-gamma, SMARCA4 by mutation burden, SMARCA4 by AXL, PTEN by ploidy, KEAP1 by TP53, and TP53 by MSI or other small contexts. The large accepted TP53-by-research-signature stratifications should be treated as features of the constructed dataset structure because the research signatures have no assigned biological role; they are not biological pathway effect modification.

CDKN2A loss remains suggestive but unsupported. Across contexts, point estimates are often around 0.13 to 0.19, but the presigned lower bounds are repeatedly below 0.15, so no CDKN2A comparison clears the meaningful-effect rule. Examples include H92, H109, H147, H155, H156, H157, H167, H177, H183, H184, H190, H200, and H201. I treat CDKN2A as a precision-limited secondary signal, not an accepted predictor.

Remaining uncertainty is mainly boundary and precision-driven. Overall EGFR amplification is small but not decisively bounded below threshold, though the clean EGFR test is negative. TP53 loss in MSI-high cells is unresolved because of small cells. PTEN loss in several high-quality clean splits remains imprecise. Rare co-occurrence contexts and small subgroup interactions remain underpowered. No validation request budget remains, so further independent confirmation cannot be obtained inside this run.

Overall conclusion: within this supplied observational dataset, the strongest scientifically meaningful evidence supports four directional associations with the composite dependency endpoint: TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss are associated with weaker dependency, while SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high are associated with stronger dependency. PTEN loss is a secondary clean-background conditional finding, and CDKN2A is suggestive but unsupported. Most driver mutations, constructed markers, technical variables, and measured biomarker interactions do not meet the effect-size threshold. The most informative next work would be external replication of the four main associations with a harmonized dependency metric, followed by targeted causal perturbation of TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, and MSI biology. In-dataset next priorities would be better-powered or multiplicity-aware models for clean-background PTEN and CDKN2A, but those cannot substitute for external or experimental validation."}

The most relevant focused interaction, H204, tested PTEN loss by ploidy within a clean background and gave a small near-null signed estimate +0.079, interval -0.078 to +0.236, unresolved and closed. H214 tested clean-background PTEN loss by high mutation burden and was rejected. Together these argue against upgrading PTEN loss to a proven major effect modifier; it should remain context-dependent and precision-limited.

Negative or non-supportive findings are substantial. Repeated main comparisons did not support a meaningful difference beyond 0.15 in either claimed direction for KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, STK11 loss, ARID1A loss, MTAP loss, RB1 loss, SMAD4 loss, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, APC mutation, PIK3CA mutation, BRAF V600E, ERBB2 amplification, and clean-background EGFR amplification. The constructed research markers D, E, and F were not associated with meaningful dependency differences. Several technical or procedural variables also failed to show meaningful differences, including Avana versus non-Avana library, matched RNA-DNA availability, media serum percentage, and the tested sex comparison. These are dataset-specific non-support findings, not proof of exact zero effects.

Interaction or effect-modification evidence is mostly negative or inconclusive. Formal biological or biomarker interaction tests were generally near null and did not clear the threshold: KEAP1 by 8q24 copy number, MSI by 8q24 copy number, PTEN by high mutation burden, KEAP1 by higher growth rate, KEAP1 by hypoxia, SMARCA4 by ARID1A, SMARCA4 by growth-rate, and several ploidy or lineage modifiers were rejected. Other interactions were unresolved but not positive evidence, including TP53 by IFN-gamma, SMARCA4 by mutation burden, SMARCA4 by AXL, PTEN by ploidy, KEAP1 by TP53, and TP53 by MSI or other small contexts. The large accepted TP53-by-research-signature stratifications should be treated as features of the constructed dataset structure because the research signatures have no assigned biological role; they are not biological pathway effect modification.

CDKN2A loss remains suggestive but unsupported. Across contexts, point estimates are often around 0.13 to 0.19, but the presigned lower bounds are repeatedly below 0.15, so no CDKN2A comparison clears the meaningful-effect rule. Examples include H92, H109, H147, H155, H156, H157, H167, H177, H183, H184, H190, H200, and H201. I treat CDKN2A as a precision-limited secondary signal, not an accepted predictor.

Remaining uncertainty is mainly boundary and precision-driven. Overall EGFR amplification is small but not decisively bounded below threshold, though the clean EGFR test is negative. TP53 loss in MSI-high cells is unresolved because of small cells. PTEN loss in several high-quality clean splits remains imprecise. Rare co-occurrence contexts and small subgroup interactions remain underpowered. No validation request budget remains, so further independent confirmation cannot be obtained inside this run.

Overall conclusion: within this supplied observational dataset, the strongest scientifically meaningful evidence supports four directional associations with the composite dependency endpoint: TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss are associated with weaker dependency, while SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high are associated with stronger dependency. PTEN loss is a secondary clean-background conditional finding, and CDKN2A is suggestive but unsupported. Most driver mutations, constructed markers, technical variables, and measured biomarker interactions do not meet the effect-size threshold. The most informative next work would be external replication of the four main associations with a harmonized dependency metric, followed by targeted causal perturbation of TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, and MSI biology. In-dataset next priorities would be better-powered or multiplicity-aware models for clean-background PTEN and CDKN2A, but those cannot substitute for external or experimental validation.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due, and no validation budget remains, so these are discovery-stage comparisons designed to refine the existing evidence map rather than request independent confirmation. The current accepted core associations are: TP53 loss associated with higher dependency_composite (weaker composite dependency), KEAP1 loss associated with higher dependency_composite, SMARCA4 loss associated with lower dependency_composite (stronger dependency), and MSI-high associated with lower dependency_composite. The first block tests whether these major associations persist in rapidly proliferating cells, defined as growth_rate_doublings_per_day >= 0.5. Expected raw exposed-minus-comparator contrasts are positive for TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss, and negative for SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high, consistent with the accepted directions. Biologically, high proliferation could attenuate or alter dependency associations by changing cell-cycle and metabolic context; alternatively, the associations may persist because the dominant genetic states still drive dependency. If any comparison is invalid because a cell has fewer than 20 observations, it should remain unresolved.

The second and third blocks test formal context stability and possible synergy. The TP53-loss by KEAP1-loss interaction in a cleaner background (MSI-high, SMARCA4 loss, and PTEN loss absent) is a refinement of H65/H20 evidence. The earlier raw interaction appeared positive: TP53 loss appeared larger in KEAP1-loss cells than in KEAP1-intact cells. Removing other dominant modifiers asks whether that positive interaction survives when confounding dominant genotypes are excluded. The KEAP1-loss by SMARCA4-loss interaction is registered with positive direction but no strong expectation; direct KEAP1 effects were already accepted both inside and outside SMARCA4-loss, so a large positive interaction is unlikely. This comparison is useful mainly to test whether KEAP1-loss effects are genuinely context-stable or whether SMARCA4-loss background modifies them beyond the 0.15-unit threshold.

The low screen_roc_auc <= 0.95 comparisons test whether accepted associations are robust to lower-quality screen performance or whether they are concentrated in high-quality screens. Expected directions are again those of the accepted main effects: TP53 and KEAP1 positive raw contrasts, SMARCA4 and MSI-high negative raw contrasts. If large effects persist even in lower-quality screens, that suggests the associations are not artifacts of high-quality screens only, but interpretation remains dataset-specific because lower-quality screens may introduce measurement error or selection effects. If effects are attenuated or invalid due small cells, that supports quality dependence rather than biological irrelevance.

The final two proposals are secondary context tests for predictors that remain precision-limited. CDKN2A loss has repeatedly produced point estimates below the 0.15 signed lower-bound threshold, but the cell-cycle relevance of CDKN2A makes rapid-growth strata biologically motivated; if the fast-growth raw contrast is negative enough and the signed lower bound exceeds 0.15, CDKN2A could become a meaningful predictor, but the prior is weak. PTEN loss is accepted in some clean genetic backgrounds but not as an unconditional main effect. Testing PTEN loss among TP53-intact fast-growing cells asks whether proliferation context can recover a PTEN association; if it does not clear the threshold, PTEN remains a secondary conditional predictor. All proposals remain observational associations in this supplied dataset and do not establish causality, mechanism, or generalizability. Decision rule remains: accept only when the signed 95% lower bound exceeds +0.15 in the claimed direction; reject when the signed upper bound is below +0.15; otherwise leave unresolved.

Iteration 17/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Interaction claims remain only for the signed direction tested; null interactions should not be interpreted as exact zero.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No assessments are due, and no validation budget remains, so these are discovery-stage comparisons designed to refine the existing evidence map rather than request independent confirmation. The current accepted core associations are: TP53 loss associated with higher dependency_composite (weaker composite dependency), KEAP1 loss associated with higher dependency_composite, SMARCA4 loss associated with lower dependency_composite (stronger dependency), and MSI-high associated with lower dependency_composite. The first block tests whether these major associations persist in rapidly proliferating cells, defined as growth_rate_doublings_per_day >= 0.5. Expected raw exposed-minus-comparator contrasts are positive for TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss, and negative for SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high, consistent with the accepted directions. Biologically, high proliferation could attenuate or alter dependency associations by changing cell-cycle and metabolic context; alternatively, the associations may persist because the dominant genetic states still drive dependency. If any comparison is invalid because a cell has fewer than 20 observations, it should remain unresolved.\n\nThe second and third blocks test formal context stability and possible synergy. The TP53-loss by KEAP1-loss interaction in a cleaner background (MSI-high, SMARCA4 loss, and PTEN loss absent) is a refinement of H65/H20 evidence. The earlier raw interaction appeared positive: TP53 loss appeared larger in KEAP1-loss cells than in KEAP1-intact cells. Removing other dominant modifiers asks whether that positive interaction survives when confounding dominant genotypes are excluded. The KEAP1-loss by SMARCA4-loss interaction is registered with positive direction but no strong expectation; direct KEAP1 effects were already accepted both inside and outside SMARCA4-loss, so a large positive interaction is unlikely. This comparison is useful mainly to test whether KEAP1-loss effects are genuinely context-stable or whether SMARCA4-loss background modifies them beyond the 0.15-unit threshold.\n\nThe low screen_roc_auc <= 0.95 comparisons test whether accepted associations are robust to lower-quality screen performance or whether they are concentrated in high-quality screens. Expected directions are again those of the accepted main effects: TP53 and KEAP1 positive raw contrasts, SMARCA4 and MSI-high negative raw contrasts. If large effects persist even in lower-quality screens, that suggests the associations are not artifacts of high-quality screens only, but interpretation remains dataset-specific because lower-quality screens may introduce measurement error or selection effects. If effects are attenuated or invalid due small cells, that supports quality dependence rather than biological irrelevance.\n\nThe final two proposals are secondary context tests for predictors that remain precision-limited. CDKN2A loss has repeatedly produced point estimates below the 0.15 signed lower-bound threshold, but the cell-cycle relevance of CDKN2A makes rapid-growth strata biologically motivated; if the fast-growth raw contrast is negative enough and the signed lower bound exceeds 0.15, CDKN2A could become a meaningful predictor, but the prior is weak. PTEN loss is accepted in some clean genetic backgrounds but not as an unconditional main effect. Testing PTEN loss among TP53-intact fast-growing cells asks whether proliferation context can recover a PTEN association; if it does not clear the threshold, PTEN remains a secondary conditional predictor. All proposals remain observational associations in this supplied dataset and do not establish causality, mechanism, or generalizability. Decision rule remains: accept only when the signed 95% lower bound exceeds +0.15 in the claimed direction; reject when the signed upper bound is below +0.15; otherwise leave unresolved.","analyze":"No assessments are due, and no new validation requests remain. I selected 12 previously registered active comparisons for analysis. H204 is the highest-priority focused follow-up because PTEN loss remains a secondary conditional predictor, and H204 directly tests whether the clean-background PTEN-loss association with stronger composite dependency is actually modified by ploidy rather than merely differing in precision across ploidy-stratified direct contrasts. H205-H208 test whether the four accepted major predictor associations persist in older adults, a demographic stratum not directly tested before. These include TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high. Some older-age cells may be small, especially for MSI-high; if any comparison cell falls below 20 observations, the result should remain unresolved rather than be interpreted. H210-H216 test candidate effect modification by biomarker state: IFN-gamma for TP53 loss, 8q24 copy number for KEAP1 loss and MSI-high, mutation burden for SMARCA4 loss, clean-context high mutation burden for PTEN loss, growth rate for KEAP1 loss, and AXL expression for SMARCA4 loss. These interactions are important because the major main effects have been context-stable across many technical and genomic strata, and formal interaction tests are needed before claiming biological or clinical modification. I deferred H209, the has_rna_omics availability check, because matched RNA-DNA availability has already been tested and was null, so this measurement-bias probe has lower incremental value than the major-predictor age and interaction tests under the 12-analysis cap. Decision rule remains prespecified: accept only when the signed lower 95% bound exceeds +0.15 composite dependency-score units in the claimed direction; reject only when the signed upper bound is below +0.15; otherwise leave unresolved. All conclusions remain dataset-specific observational associations on the composite dependency endpoint, not causal effects or generalizable biological mechanisms.","appraise":"I assessed the newly delivered discovery evidence with the prespecified signed-bound rule: accept only when the signed 95% lower bound exceeds +0.15 composite dependency-score units in the claimed direction; reject when the signed upper bound is below +0.15; otherwise leave unresolved. All estimates are already signed to the hypothesis direction, so they were not re-oriented.\n\nH204 is the focused clean-background PTEN-loss interaction with higher ploidy. The signed interaction estimate was +0.0788 with interval -0.0785 to +0.2362. It does not clear the +0.15 lower-bound threshold, and it also is not precise enough to reject by the upper-bound rule. I therefore left it unresolved but closed the investigation because the point estimate is small, the comparison is already multiplicity-adjusted for the overall PTEN line, and no validation request is available. This result gives no support for the stronger claim that PTEN loss is materially modified by ploidy within the clean background; it should not be used to upgrade PTEN loss from a secondary conditional predictor to a major effect modifier.\n\nThe older-adult age strata were strongly informative. H205, TP53 loss in participants with age_years >= 65, was accepted: signed estimate +0.5181, interval +0.3176 to +0.7185. This supports persistence of the accepted TP53-loss association with weaker composite dependency in this older-adult subset. H206, KEAP1 loss in age_years >= 65, was also accepted: signed estimate +0.8313, interval +0.6453 to +1.0174, supporting the accepted KEAP1-loss association with weaker composite dependency. H207, SMARCA4 loss in age_years >= 65, was accepted: signed estimate +0.7205, interval +0.5281 to +0.9129, corresponding to the claimed stronger-dependency direction. H208, MSI-high in age_years >= 65, was accepted: signed estimate +0.8762, interval +0.6006 to +1.1517, also corresponding to stronger dependency. Together these age-stratified results materially increase confidence that the four major predictor associations are not confined to younger or non-older subsets within this dataset. However, age_years is missing for a substantial fraction of the sample, and the exposed cells are relatively small, especially MSI-high with 23 exposed cases. These are therefore dataset-specific observational associations subject to selection bias and age-missingness, not causal age effects or externally generalizable demographic claims.\n\nThe biomarker interaction panel mostly did not support effect modification. H210, TP53 loss by IFN-gamma state, was unresolved: signed estimate +0.1090, interval -0.0836 to +0.3016. Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

The current accepted core associations are: TP53 loss associated with higher dependency_composite (weaker composite dependency), KEAP1 loss associated with higher dependency_composite, SMARCA4 loss associated with lower dependency_composite (stronger dependency), and MSI-high associated with lower dependency_composite. The first block tests whether these major associations persist in rapidly proliferating cells, defined as growth_rate_doublings_per_day >= 0.5. Expected raw exposed-minus-comparator contrasts are positive for TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss, and negative for SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high, consistent with the accepted directions. Biologically, high proliferation could attenuate or alter dependency associations by changing cell-cycle and metabolic context; alternatively, the associations may persist because the dominant genetic states still drive dependency. If any comparison is invalid because a cell has fewer than 20 observations, it should remain unresolved.\n\nThe second and third blocks test formal context stability and possible synergy. The TP53-loss by KEAP1-loss interaction in a cleaner background (MSI-high, SMARCA4 loss, and PTEN loss absent) is a refinement of H65/H20 evidence. The earlier raw interaction appeared positive: TP53 loss appeared larger in KEAP1-loss cells than in KEAP1-intact cells. Removing other dominant modifiers asks whether that positive interaction survives when confounding dominant genotypes are excluded. The KEAP1-loss by SMARCA4-loss interaction is registered with positive direction but no strong expectation; direct KEAP1 effects were already accepted both inside and outside SMARCA4-loss, so a large positive interaction is unlikely. This comparison is useful mainly to test whether KEAP1-loss effects are genuinely context-stable or whether SMARCA4-loss background modifies them beyond the 0.15-unit threshold.\n\nThe low screen_roc_auc <= 0.95 comparisons test whether accepted associations are robust to lower-quality screen performance or whether they are concentrated in high-quality screens. Expected directions are again those of the accepted main effects: TP53 and KEAP1 positive raw contrasts, SMARCA4 and MSI-high negative raw contrasts. If large effects persist even in lower-quality screens, that suggests the associations are not artifacts of high-quality screens only, but interpretation remains dataset-specific because lower-quality screens may introduce measurement error or selection effects. If effects are attenuated or invalid due small cells, that supports quality dependence rather than biological irrelevance.\n\nThe final two proposals are secondary context tests for predictors that remain precision-limited. CDKN2A loss has repeatedly produced point estimates below the 0.15 signed lower-bound threshold, but the cell-cycle relevance of CDKN2A makes rapid-growth strata biologically motivated; if the fast-growth raw contrast is negative enough and the signed lower bound exceeds 0.15, CDKN2A could become a meaningful predictor, but the prior is weak. record.narrative:
I assessed all newly delivered discovery results using the prespecified signed-bound decision rule on the composite dependency-score scale: accept only if the signed 95% lower bound exceeds +0.15 in the claimed direction, reject only if the signed upper bound is below +0.15, and otherwise leave unresolved. All estimates were already signed to the hypothesis direction, so I did not re-orient them. No independent validation was requested because the remaining new validation-request budget is zero.

Measurement-artifact check: H209 tested whether RNA-omics availability was associated with a higher composite score. The signed estimate was -0.0275 (interval -0.1167 to +0.0616). The positive-direction claim is not supported, and the upper bound is below the 0.15 meaningfulness threshold, so I rejected H209 and closed it. This is not evidence that RNA-omics availability is exactly unrelated to the outcome, but it is evidence against a large positive measurement-availability artifact in the claimed direction within this supplied dataset.

Fast-proliferation robustness: The four major accepted associations persisted in the fast-growth stratum. H217 (TP53 loss, growth rate >= 0.5) had signed estimate +0.4985, interval +0.3474 to +0.6497; H218 (KEAP1 loss) +0.7627, +0.6438 to +0.8816; H219 (SMARCA4 loss, direction -1) +0.8077, +0.6887 to +0.9268; H220 (MSI-high, direction -1) +0.8460, +0.6963 to +0.9958. All signed lower bounds exceeded +0.15, so I accepted and closed these. This strengthens internal dataset-specific robustness of the four core associations among rapidly proliferating cells. However, acceptance of direct stratum effects does not establish positive effect modification by proliferation rate; formal growth-rate interaction tests were not positive for the relevant comparisons, and the direct fast-stratum acceptance only says the association is detectable in that stratum.

Lower screen-quality robustness: H223-H226 tested the same four major predictors among lower-quality screens (screen_roc_auc <= 0.95). H223 TP53 loss +0.3602, interval +0.1999 to +0.5205; H224 KEAP1 loss +0.8963, +0.7932 to +0.9994; H225 SMARCA4 loss +0.8409, +0.7392 to +0.9426; H226 MSI-high +0.8806, +0.6813 to +1.0799. All signed lower bounds exceeded +0.15, so I accepted and closed these. The core associations are not confined to high-quality screens within this dataset. I did not treat this as evidence that lower-quality screens introduce no bias or error; rather, it shows the main associations remain large and directionally stable in the lower-quality subset. No formal positive screen-quality interaction is implied by these direct stratum estimates.

KEAP1-SMARCA4 interaction: H222 was near null (signed +0.0233, interval -0.1206 to +0.1672). The interval does not satisfy the accept rule and is not sufficiently bounded below the threshold to reject strictly under the rule because the upper bound is slightly above +0.15. I therefore marked it unresolved but closed the investigation. Given that direct KEAP1-loss effects have been accepted in both SMARCA4-loss and SMARCA4-intact backgrounds, and this interaction is centered near zero, I would not interpret H222 as evidence of meaningful KEAP1-SMARCA4 interaction on the dependency_composite endpoint.

Secondary predictors: H227 CDKN2A loss in fast-growing cells was not supported: signed +0.0839, interval -0.0502 to +0.2180. The point estimate is small, the lower bound is below zero, and the comparison does not clear the 0.15-unit accept threshold. I left it unresolved under the formal rule but closed the investigation because CDKN2A has repeatedly remained precision-limited across many contexts and validation budget is exhausted. H228 PTEN loss among TP53-intact fast-growing cells gave signed estimate +0.3039, interval +0.1545 to +0.4532. This narrowly clears the signed lower-bound threshold, so I accepted and closed it. The accept is dataset-specific, context-specific, and borderline; PTEN loss remains a secondary conditional predictor rather than an unconditional major predictor, especially given the many related PTEN comparisons, boundary lower bound, and lack of remaining validation budget.

Overall, this batch strengthens internal robustness of the four main dataset-specific associations: TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss associated with higher composite dependency scores (weaker composite dependency), and SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high associated with lower scores (stronger composite dependency). It also rejects a large positive RNA-omics-availability artifact in the tested direction and shows that the major associations are not confined to high-quality screens. It does not support meaningful KEAP1-SMARCA4 interaction, CDKN2A fast-growth effect, or growth/quality effect modification from these direct stratum tests. These remain observational associations in the supplied dataset, not causal effects, mechanisms, or generalizable claims.

prompt:
Iteration 17/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.
