record.narrative:
Applied the prespecified signed rule: accept only when the signed 95% lower bound exceeds +0.15 composite dependency-score units; reject only when the signed upper bound is below +0.15; otherwise unresolved. All twelve new results are valid Welch independent-cell comparisons and no analysis cell is below 20 observations, but they remain unadjusted and occur within a heavily multiplicity-burdened exploratory program, so conclusions are dataset-specific and noncausal.

H250, H251, and H252 are accepted. TP53-loss, KEAP1-loss, and SMARCA4-loss contrasts persist in the has_rna_omics=0 subgroup: TP53-loss signed +0.512 [0.262,0.761], KEAP1-loss signed +0.973 [0.793,1.153], and SMARCA4-loss signed +0.814 [0.612,1.017]. This is robustness within the supplied data only: the has_rna_omics=0 cells are relatively small and may be confounded by technical batch, library, screen-quality, or other correlated dataset features. The results do not imply causality or external generalizability.

H253 and H255 are unresolved. The formal lower-screen-quality interactions for KEAP1-loss and MSI-high are +0.110 [-0.024,0.243] and +0.133 [-0.111,0.376], respectively; each interval includes values below +0.15. H254 is rejected as evidence of a meaningful lower-screen-quality interaction for SMARCA4-loss because the signed estimate is +0.014 and the signed upper bound +0.147 is just below +0.15. These results should not be conflated with earlier accepted direct effects in lower-quality screen strata: direct stratum acceptance is not evidence of effect modification.

PTEN loss remains a secondary, context-dependent association rather than a general main predictor. H256 is accepted in the cleaner TP53-intact, KEAP1-intact, SMARCA4-intact, MSI-nonhigh, CDKN2A-intact, Avana background: signed +0.307 [0.216,0.398]. H257 also passes the prespecified rule in the analogous cleaner background restricted to lower screen quality, signed +0.306 [0.158,0.455], but the lower bound is barely above threshold and the cell count is smaller; it should be treated as supportive but fragile conditional evidence. H258 shows no established growth-rate interaction among TP53-intact cells, signed +0.042 [-0.157,0.241]. H261 is unresolved in the direct adherent growth-pattern stratum, signed +0.251 [0.140,0.363], because the lower bound does not clear +0.15. The adherent stratum is not genetically clean and may be diluted by stronger modifiers such as TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, or MSI status.

H259 remains unresolved. The high-cut research_signature_b interaction for SMARCA4-loss is signed +0.146 [-0.008,0.299]; it is suggestive but does not clear the threshold and should be interpreted only as a constructed-assay structure feature, not as biological pathway modification.

H260 is accepted. MSI-high shows a large lower-dependency association in adherent growth_pattern, signed +0.873 [0.740,1.007], consistent with the main MSI-high finding and earlier stratum analyses. This direct stratum result supports persistence of the MSI-high association in the dominant growth-pattern context but is not interaction evidence. H261 does not clear the same threshold for PTEN loss and remains unresolved.

All due lines are closed because validation is exhausted and further subgroup mining would mainly increase multiplicity without resolving precision-limited questions. The strongest conclusions remain the dataset-specific main associations for TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high, with PTEN as a secondary conditional finding and CDKN2A and most other measured predictors remaining unsupported or precision-limited.

prompt:
Iteration 20/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due, and independent-validation request capacity remains exhausted, so this exploration uses the remaining discovery budget for targeted follow-up of already supported signals, a few residual technical robustness questions, and a limited set of direct continuous-expression hypotheses rather than broad subgroup mining. The goal is to test whether the accepted dataset-specific associations for TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high are also meaningful in the dominant adherent growth-pattern context, whether their estimated contrasts differ formally across RNA-omics availability, and whether a small number of biologically interpretable RNA-expression predictors have main associations with dependency_composite. PTEN is also refined because it is currently a secondary context-dependent finding rather than an unconditional main predictor.

I register direct TP53-loss, KEAP1-loss, and SMARCA4-loss comparisons restricted to growth_pattern='adherent'. These are new direct stratum tests, not the earlier adherent growth_pattern interactions. Scientific rationale: adherent growth is the dominant culture/growth context, and prior direct stratum analyses included MSI-high and PTEN in adherent cells but did not test the main genetic modifiers directly in this large context. Expected raw directions follow the accepted main associations: TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss should produce more positive exposed-minus-comparator differences (higher composite score, i.e., weaker composite dependency), while SMARCA4 loss should produce a more negative raw contrast (lower composite score, i.e., stronger composite dependency). Plausible alternatives are attenuation, confounding by other correlated context features, or no scientifically meaningful stratum effect.

I then register formal has_rna_omics=0 versus has_rna_omics=1 interactions for TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, and MSI-high. The direct has_rna_omics=0 strata were accepted and appeared somewhat larger for KEAP1 and SMARCA4, but direct within-stratum acceptance is not evidence of effect modification. These interaction claims test whether the observed association is systematically larger among samples lacking RNA-omics coverage. Expected directions match the raw stratum pattern: TP53 and KEAP1 raw interactions are claimed to be more positive in no-RNA samples; SMARCA4 and MSI raw interactions are claimed to be more negative in no-RNA samples. Anticipation is intentionally uncertain because the no-RNA subset is small and could reflect assay coverage, batch, sample type, or biology. Alternatives include no interaction, attenuation, or opposite direction due to confounding. These are technical/biological robustness checks, not evidence that RNA-omics itself causes the dependency-score association.

I register three direct high-versus-low RNA-expression comparisons: MYC, AXL, and SLFN11. These are intended as continuous-expression biomarker hypotheses rather than causal genetic-dependency statements. MYC high (approximately >=6 log2 TPM) versus low (<=4) is claimed in the lower-composite direction, reflecting possible transcriptional oncogenic state or dependency, with the alternative that high MYC expression may reflect proliferation without dependency or even weaker composite dependency. AXL high (>=4) versus low (<=2) is claimed in the higher-composite direction, reflecting a plausible resistant or less strongly dependent phenotype, with alternatives of lower or null association. SLFN11 high (>=4.5) versus low (<=3) is claimed in the lower-composite direction, reflecting a plausible stronger dependency associated with DNA-damage-response biology, with alternatives of no association or weaker dependency. These tests remain dataset-specific observational associations on a composite endpoint; expression thresholds are chosen to retain adequate cell counts but are not validated biomarker cut points.

Finally, I refine PTEN in two context-dependent directions. First, I restrict the accepted clean genetic adenocarcinoma background by high screen quality (screen_roc_auc >= 0.96), testing whether the conditional PTEN association persists when screen quality is better. Second, I test PTEN loss in a genetically clean background excluding Avana libraries, complementing the accepted Avana-restricted PTEN comparison. PTEN is not supported as an unconditional main predictor at the 0.15 threshold; these proposals ask whether its association is narrow or reproducible across cleaner technical contexts. Expected raw direction is lower composite score for PTEN loss where the association persists, but non-Avana sample sizes may be limited. Alternatives include attenuation, invalid cells due to small counts, or a context-specific association that disappears outside the previously accepted Avana or clean adenocarcinoma setting.

All proposals remain evaluated under the prespecified signed decision rule: accept only if the signed 95% lower bound exceeds +0.15 composite dependency-score units, reject only if the signed upper bound is below +0.15, otherwise leave unresolved; invalid cells with fewer than 20 observations will not be interpreted. Because independent validation is exhausted, these are discovery-only dataset-specific observational comparisons. They can support reproducibility within selected contexts but cannot establish causality, biological mechanism, or external generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 21/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

H269-H271 test direct high-versus-low RNA-expression contrasts for MYC, AXL, and SLFN11 on the composite dependency endpoint. These are dataset-specific observational comparisons and do not establish causality, mechanism, or external generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 21/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment

These are new direct stratum tests, not the earlier adherent growth_pattern interactions. Scientific rationale: adherent growth is the dominant culture/growth context, and prior direct stratum analyses included MSI-high and PTEN in adherent cells but did not test the main genetic modifiers directly in this large context. Expected raw directions follow the accepted main associations: TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss should produce more positive exposed-minus-comparator differences (higher composite score, i.e., weaker composite dependency), while SMARCA4 loss should produce a more negative raw contrast (lower composite score, i.e., stronger composite dependency). Plausible alternatives are attenuation, confounding by other correlated context features, or no scientifically meaningful stratum effect.\n\nI then register formal has_rna_omics=0 versus has_rna_omics=1 interactions for TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, and MSI-high. The direct has_rna_omics=0 strata were accepted and appeared somewhat larger for KEAP1 and SMARCA4, but direct within-stratum acceptance is not evidence of effect modification. These interaction claims test whether the observed association is systematically larger among samples lacking RNA-omics coverage. Expected directions match the raw stratum pattern: TP53 and KEAP1 raw interactions are claimed to be more positive in no-RNA samples; SMARCA4 and MSI raw interactions are claimed to be more negative in no-RNA samples. Anticipation is intentionally uncertain because the no-RNA subset is small and could reflect assay coverage, batch, sample type, or biology. Alternatives include no interaction, attenuation, or opposite direction due to confounding. These are technical/biological robustness checks, not evidence that RNA-omics itself causes the dependency-score association.\n\nI register three direct high-versus-low RNA-expression comparisons: MYC, AXL, and SLFN11. These are intended as continuous-expression biomarker hypotheses rather than causal genetic-dependency statements. MYC high (approximately >=6 log2 TPM) versus low (<=4) is claimed in the lower-composite direction, reflecting possible transcriptional oncogenic state or dependency, with the alternative that high MYC expression may reflect proliferation without dependency or even weaker composite dependency. AXL high (>=4) versus low (<=2) is claimed in the higher-composite direction, reflecting a plausible resistant or less strongly dependent phenotype, with alternatives of lower or null association. SLFN11 high (>=4.5) versus low (<=3) is claimed in the lower-composite direction, reflecting a plausible stronger dependency associated with DNA-damage-response biology, with alternatives of no association or weaker dependency. These tests remain dataset-specific observational associations on a composite endpoint; expression thresholds are chosen to retain adequate cell counts but are not validated biomarker cut points.\n\nFinally, I refine PTEN in two context-dependent directions. First, I restrict the accepted clean genetic adenocarcinoma background by high screen quality (screen_roc_auc >= 0.96), testing whether the conditional PTEN association persists when screen quality is better. Second, I test PTEN loss in a genetically clean background excluding Avana libraries, complementing the accepted Avana-restricted PTEN comparison. PTEN is not supported as an unconditional main predictor at the 0.15 threshold; these proposals ask whether its association is narrow or reproducible across cleaner technical contexts. Expected raw direction is lower composite score for PTEN loss where the association persists, but non-Avana sample sizes may be limited. However, within-stratum acceptance is not evidence of effect modification. Formal interaction tests were generally unresolved, non-supportive, or limited to constructed assay structure. In particular, accepted interactions involving research_signature_a, research_signature_b, or research_signature_c should not be interpreted as biological pathway modification because these signatures have no assigned biological role.\n\nSecondary conditional PTEN finding: PTEN loss is not supported as a general unconditional association at the prespecified effect-size threshold. The overall comparison is precision-limited in the negative-dependency direction: signed evidence R36 is +0.227 with lower bound +0.131 and validation R65 is +0.226 with lower bound +0.087. In contrast, multiple cleaner genetic backgrounds show accepted conditional PTEN-loss associations toward lower dependency_composite, especially when TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, MSI-high, and other strong modifiers are absent, or in selected Avana and lower-quality screen backgrounds. These conditional effects commonly have signed estimates around 0.2 to 0.4 units, but the evidence remains context-dependent and hypothesis-generating rather than primary.\n\nNegative or non-supportive findings: KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, STK11 loss, ARID1A loss, MTAP loss, RB1 loss, SMAD4 loss, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, APC mutation, PIK3CA mutation, BRAF V600E, ERBB2 amplification, clean-background EGFR amplification, constructed markers d/e/f, sex, media serum, has_rna_omics, has_matched_rna_dna, and several technical availability or library contrasts did not meet the meaningful-effect criterion in the tested directions. TP53-loss effects in non-Avana contexts and in MSI-high cells remain imprecise. Several lower-screen-quality, growth-pattern, signature, batch, and interaction hypotheses remain unresolved because intervals include values below the effect threshold. record.narrative:
Applying the prespecified signed rule, H262-H264 are accepted. TP53-loss, KEAP1-loss, and SMARCA4-loss associations remain scientifically meaningful in the adherent growth-pattern stratum: TP53 +0.432 [0.321, 0.542], KEAP1 +0.877 [0.803, 0.951], and SMARCA4 +0.851 [0.772, 0.930]. These are robustness confirmations in a large dominant stratum, not new independent discovery: growth_pattern is collinear with culture/growth and other dataset features, and these are unadjusted subgroup contrasts. Acceptance does not imply causality or effect modification.

The formal has_rna_omics interactions H265-H267 are unresolved. TP53 +0.107 [-0.163, 0.377], KEAP1 +0.168 [-0.025, 0.361], and SMARCA4 -0.022 [-0.235, 0.191] do not provide evidence of meaningful effect modification by RNA-omics availability. H268 is invalid because one interaction cell has 19 observations; no conclusion can be made about MSI-high modification by has_rna_omics.

H269-H271 are invalid because the continuous-expression high-versus-low contrasts produced zero observation cells, likely due to a specification/coding limitation rather than an empirical null: exact exposed/comparator values for continuous assays are not equivalent to thresholded high/low groups. Thus MYC, AXL, and SLFN11 main-expression associations remain not assessed, not negative.

H272 remains unresolved: PTEN-loss in the high-quality adenocarcinoma clean background has signed estimate +0.162 [0.021, 0.303], which is near threshold but has insufficient precision. H273 is invalid because the non-Avana comparison has only 14 exposed observations. PTEN therefore remains a secondary, context-dependent signal and should not be elevated to a general main predictor. Validation request capacity is exhausted; these are dataset-specific observational associations only. No new proposals are registered to avoid further exploratory subgroup mining.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Iteration 21/25, stage synthesize, attempt 2.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
No new validation result is present in this stage, no response deadline is open, and voluntary validation request capacity is exhausted. The only scientific correction needed is a canonical reassessment of the TP53-loss by KEAP1-loss clean-background interaction comparison. H136 and H221 represent the same canonical scientific comparison, so I assess only the canonical H136 rather than submitting duplicate assessments. The available evidence is discovery R119, signed estimate +0.116 [-0.093, 0.324], and independent validation R131, signed estimate -0.032 [-0.404, 0.340]. Applying the signed decision rule against the 0.15 composite-unit threshold, neither interval is wholly above +0.15 nor wholly below +0.15. Therefore the interaction is neither supported nor convincingly ruled out; the earlier reject was too strong, and the correct status is unresolved. I close the internal investigation because additional discovery-only subgroup refinement would not add decisive information and validation capacity is exhausted. Final scientific report follows.

Supported main predictors in this supplied dataset. The strongest and most stable dataset-specific associations are four predictors that clear the 0.15 threshold in their claimed directions and have independent validation: TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high. TP53 loss is associated with a higher dependency_composite value, meaning weaker composite dependency under the convention that more negative values indicate stronger dependency: H13/R1 gives +0.423 [0.327, 0.520] and validation R38 gives +0.355 [0.221, 0.488]. KEAP1 loss shows the largest positive-score association, also toward weaker composite dependency: H14/R5 gives +0.832 [0.766, 0.897] and validation R25 gives +0.769 [0.676, 0.862]. SMARCA4 loss is associated with lower dependency_composite values, meaning stronger composite dependency; the signed negative-direction claim H62/R32 gives +0.833 [0.767, 0.898], and validation R52 gives +0.817 [0.715, 0.918]. MSI-high is similarly associated with lower composite scores, meaning stronger dependency: H106/R86 gives +0.792 [0.676, 0.907], and validation R105 gives +0.873 [0.685, 1.060]. These are associations within the supplied dataset on a composite dependency endpoint. They are not evidence of causal genetic effects, not single-gene dependency statements, and not established mechanistic claims.

Robustness and context. The accepted main associations are broad within this dataset. They remain supported in adenocarcinoma, the dominant adherent growth context, growth-rate strata, screen-quality strata, CRISPR-library strata, batch_a where adequately powered, older adults, selected cleaner genetic backgrounds, and samples without RNA-omics coverage. Examples include TP53-loss strata R18, R15, R20, R248; KEAP1-loss strata R19, R16, R21, R249; SMARCA4-loss strata R47, R129, R130, R250; and MSI-high strata R95, R246. However, acceptance within strata is not the same as evidence of effect modification. Formal interaction tests were mostly unresolved or should be interpreted as technical data partitions rather than biology. In particular, the newly corrected clean-background TP53 by KEAP1 interaction remains unresolved. Some accepted interactions involve constructed research_signature_a, research_signature_b, or research_signature_c, or technical growth-pattern structure; because those variables have no assigned biological role and are collinear with other dataset features, they should not be read as pathway or mechanism. The latest formal has_rna_omics interactions H265-H267 were also unresolved, and H268 was invalid because of small cells, so assay-coverage modification is not established.

Secondary context-dependent PTEN signal. PTEN loss is not supported as a general unconditional predictor at the prespecified effect-size threshold. The overall negative-dependency direction is precision-limited: signed R36 is +0.227 [0.131, 0.323], and validation R65 is +0.226 [0.087, 0.364], both failing the signed lower-bound rule by a modest margin. In several cleaner conditional backgrounds, however, PTEN loss is associated with lower dependency_composite values, meaning stronger dependency, and multiple comparisons are accepted: for example, without TP53 loss R50 is +0.259 [0.169, 0.349] with validation R92 +0.297 [0.168, 0.426], and in a TP53/KEAP1/SMARCA4/MSI-negative clean background R66 is +0.252 [0.169, 0.335] with validation R78 +0.263 [0.135, 0.392]. Similar conditional accepted effects appear when MSI-high, PIK3CA mutation, or other modifiers are absent. These PTEN results are best described as secondary, context-dependent, and hypothesis-generating, not a primary main effect.

Negative or non-supportive findings. Many tested predictors did not meet the meaningful-effect criterion in the tested directions. These include KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, STK11 loss, ARID1A loss, MTAP loss, RB1 loss, SMAD4 loss, BRCA2 loss, NF1 loss, APC mutation, PIK3CA mutation, BRAF V600E, ERBB2 amplification, constructed research markers d/e/f, sex, media serum percentage, has_rna_omics, has_matched_rna_dna, and the main Avana-library contrast after validation. Clean-background EGFR amplification is also non-supportive, though the broader EGFR amplification contrast remains unresolved. These are non-support results in this dataset, not proof of zero effects in other populations or assay settings.

Unresolved and invalid comparisons. CDKN2A loss remains suggestive but not generally supported. Multiple CDKN2A estimates are near the 0.15 threshold, including R34 +0.141 [0.062, 0.220], R142 +0.153 [0.092, 0.215], R143 +0.149 [0.050, 0.247], R154 +0.186 [0.081, 0.292], and related subgroup comparisons, but the interval pattern does not consistently clear the signed threshold. TP53 loss in non-Avana libraries and in MSI-high cells remains imprecise: R26 is +0.366 [0.063, 0.669] but validation R106 is +0.098 [-0.393, 0.589], and R159 is +0.301 [-0.129, 0.732]. Many interaction hypotheses, including several signature, growth-pattern, screen-quality, ploidy, aneuploidy, and technical-availability interactions, remain unresolved. The clean-background TP53 by KEAP1 interaction is now explicitly unresolved as assessed above. Some comparisons are invalid because of insufficient cell counts or specification issues and should not be read as null: the high-versus-low continuous expression contrasts for MYC, AXL, and SLFN11 produced zero-cell comparisons; H268 and H273 have cells below 20; H181, H268, H270, H271, and H273 are invalid or underpowered.

Inferential boundaries and most informative next analysis. The conclusions are limited to associations in this supplied dataset. Unadjusted Welch comparisons, multiplicity, conditional eligibility and possible collider sensitivity, collinearity among growth_pattern, culture, batch, lineage, library, and screen-quality features, missing covariates, and the composite nature of dependency_composite all limit causal interpretation. The most informative next analysis is external replication using an independently sampled or differently measured dependency phenotype, ideally combined with orthogonal perturbation of TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, MSI biology, and the PTEN conditional context. If expression hypotheses are revisited internally, they should be prespecified and recoded as adequately powered high-versus-low groups rather than exact continuous-value contrasts. A prespecified formal test of the TP53 by KEAP1 clean-background interaction, with multivariable adjustment for batch, library, growth pattern, screen quality, and lineage, would be a more focused internal next step, but current internal subgroup mining is unlikely to add decisive information beyond the supported main associations and secondary PTEN context signal.

Iteration 22/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units

record.narrative: No assessments are due, and independent-validation request capacity is exhausted, so this exploration registers targeted discovery-only refinements. First, I refine the canonical TP53-loss by KEAP1-loss interaction within high screen quality (screen_roc_auc >= 0.96). Direct strata suggested larger effects in the combined-loss/high-quality setting, but the overall interaction and the prior clean-background interaction remain unresolved; this is a prespecified refinement rather than new subgroup mining. Second, I add two PTEN-loss refinements because PTEN is a secondary context-dependent signal rather than an unconditional main predictor: a non-Avana technical context and a high screen-quality context. Third, I correct the earlier invalid continuous-expression claims by testing expression contexts through valid interaction subgroups rather than exact continuous exposed/comparator values. I use approximately upper-quartile thresholds for MYC (>=5.5), AXL (>=4.0), and SLFN11 (>=4.25) log2 TPM to maintain adequate cell counts. The expression interaction claims test whether measured RNA-expression context modifies the accepted main genetic associations in the direction of the main raw association; attenuation or no modification are explicit alternatives. These are dataset-specific observational contrasts on a composite endpoint, not expression main effects, and do not establish causality, mechanism, or generalizability. All new claims remain unresolved at registration and will be assessed under the signed rule against the 0.15 composite-unit threshold.

prompt:
Iteration 22/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

I therefore use the current analysis capacity to test the 12 active discovery-only comparisons registered in the latest exploration: H274 through H285. H274 is a focused refinement of the clean-background TP53-loss by KEAP1-loss interaction within high-quality screens, testing whether the unresolved interaction is clarified under the high screen-quality context. H275 and H276 test secondary PTEN-loss associations in technical/screen-quality contexts rather than elevating PTEN to a general main predictor. H277 through H285 test expression-context modification using prespecified upper-quartile-like thresholds for MYC, AXL, and SLFN11, now specified as adequately powered high-expression interactions rather than invalid exact continuous-value contrasts. Results will be interpreted under the same signed rule: accept only if the signed 95% Welch lower bound exceeds +0.15 composite dependency-score units, reject only if the signed upper bound is below +0.15, otherwise leave unresolved; invalid cell-count comparisons will not be treated as empirical nulls. Positive interaction estimates should be interpreted cautiously as possible context modification, assay coverage, selection, batch, or confounding structure rather than causal effect modification. All requested analyses remain dataset-specific observational contrasts on a composite dependency endpoint.
